Carlton from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending April 30, 1940". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires that Charles J. Carlton, who "was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending April 30, 1939, by Executive Order No. 7876 of April 26, 1938", be further exempted; the order is a further exemption of an employee already exempted by earlier orders, which are separate instruments. The command is a time-limited permission for one named employee, so it ended by its own terms on April 30, 1940; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day), and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. No later event is recorded for this clause: no held order text revokes, amends, extends or otherwise cites this order (see the earlier-end check). MOMMSEN-I rechecked this stated end against both held witnesses. APP has 1 hereby and conipulsorv where GPO has I hereby and compulsory.
